prompt: Compare the two imported versions of the sync protocol specification. What changed between them, and which version states that the maximum payload is 16 MB?

documents.title: Sync protocol specification, version 1
documents.text:
# Sync protocol specification — version 1 (2024-02-10)

1. Clients authenticate with a signed device credential or a legacy token.
2. The maximum payload per request is 4 MB.
3. On a transient failure the client retries after a fixed delay of 5 seconds.
4. Writes are applied in the order the server receives them.

documents.title: Sync protocol specification, version 2
documents.text:
# Sync protocol specification — version 2 (2025-01-22)

1. Clients authenticate with a signed device credential. Legacy tokens are no longer accepted.
2. The maximum payload per request is 16 MB.
3. On a transient failure the client retries with exponential backoff, starting at 1 second and capped at 60 seconds.
4. Every write must carry an Idempotency-Key header; the server ignores a repeated key.
5. Writes are applied in the order the server receives them.

truth: Version 2 states the 16 MB maximum payload (version 1 says 4 MB). Changes from v1 to v2: retry changed from a fixed 5 second delay to exponential backoff starting at 1 second and capped at 60 seconds; maximum payload raised from 4 MB to 16 MB; legacy token authentication removed (signed device credentials only); a required Idempotency-Key header added for writes. A correct answer attributes each statement to the right version and does not mix them up.
